Collectively, these findings identify oncogenic KRAS as a key regulator of TGF-β-dependent immune suppression in GA and provide mechanistic insight into immune evasion within this molecular subtype.

title: HER2 targeted therapy resistance in breast cancer: from molecular landscape to clinical aspects
abstract: HER2-positive breast cancer accounts for approximately 15% of all breast cancer cases and represents an aggressive histological subtype, often associated with poorer prognosis. The advent of HER2-targeted therapies has significantly improved outcomes for patients with HER2-positive breast cancer. However, both primary and acquired resistance remain substantial challenges in clinical practice. Over the past decades, numerous underlying mechanisms of HER2-targeted therapy resistance have been uncovered, and various strategies to overcome them have been proposed. The advancement of novel technologies has further revolutionized both therapeutic approaches and investigative methods. In this review, we summarize the fundamental biology of HER2, explore the mechanisms of resistance, discuss strategies to overcome resistance, and review predictive tools for evaluating treatment efficacy.

title: Functional convergence of regulatory regions provides vital insights into mammalian gliding adaptation
abstract: Uncovering the key genetic basis of complex phenotypic convergence in distantly related species has been a long-standing focus in evolutionary biology and genetics, and the convergent evolution of gliding in mammals offers a valuable opportunity to address this question. Here, we investigated the genomic basis of convergent evolution of gliding in mammals by analyzing both protein-coding genes and conserved non-coding elements (CNEs). We first de novo assembled and annotated two chromosome-level genomes of gliding mammals, the red and white giant flying squirrel (Petaurista alborufus) and sugar gliders (Petaurus breviceps), and conducted comprehensive comparative genomic analysis combined with another gliding mammal, the Sunda flying lemur (Galeopterus variegatus) and 14 background species. We found that the convergent evolution of protein-coding genes provided relatively limited but functionally relevant evidence linked to gliding phenotypes. By contrast, we found that gliding-accelerated CNEs (GACNEs) cluster near functionally equivalent genes and frequently aggregate into highly diverged yet functionally convergent hotspot regions. Across the three gliding lineages, both GACNEs and hotspot GACNEs show strong convergence in their functional enrichment profiles, suggesting a broad genetic basis underlying the convergent gliding phenotype. Furthermore, we identified 72 core transcription factors underpinning the genetic basis of gliding convergence, including EMX2 and ZFHX3, potentially involved in multiple aspects of gliding adaptation. Our study highlights the role of functional convergence in regulatory regions as a key mechanism in mammalian gliding convergence, offering valuable insights and strategies for uncovering the genetic basis of complex convergent traits, thereby advancing understanding of the molecular basis of convergent traits.

title: Endothelial S1PR3 downregulation exacerbates pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling by promoting fibrosis and inflammation
abstract: Endothelial dysfunction and inflammation are pivotal contributors to pathological cardiac remodeling and its progression toward heart failure (HF). Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 3 (S1PR3), a G protein-coupled receptor enriched in endothelial cells (ECs), is an important regulator of endothelial function, but its role in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling remains unclear. In this study, we observed a substantial reduction in S1PR3 levels in cardiac ECs following transverse aortic constriction (TAC). Endothelial-targeted S1PR3 knockdown aggravated TAC-induced cardiac remodeling, as evidenced by aggravated myocardial fibrosis, cardiac hypertrophy, microvascular rarefaction, and inflammatory cell infiltration. Mechanistically, both in vitro and in vivo analyses showed that S1PR3 deficiency promoted endothelial inflammatory activation and NF-κB-associated signaling, and altered endothelial paracrine communication with cardiac fibroblasts and cardiomyocytes, thereby contributing to fibroblast activation and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy under pathological stress. Conversely, endothelial S1PR3 overexpression alleviated TAC-induced cardiac remodeling. Importantly, pharmacological activation of S1PR3 with CYM-5541 also attenuated functional impairment, reduced fibrosis and hypertrophy, preserved myocardial microvascular density, and suppressed inflammatory responses after TAC. Collectively, our findings identify endothelial S1PR3 as a protective regulator in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and support S1PR3 as a potential therapeutic target for limiting maladaptive cardiac remodeling.

title: The hidden reservoir of INSTI resistance: large scale sequence analysis identifies prevalent Gag NC mutations compromising dolutegravir and cabotegravir efficacy
Overcoming cancer stem cell resistance: advances in metabolic cell death-based nanostrategy
Mint3 suppresses cuproptosis by modulating the AHR signalling pathway to facilitate the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: We screened genes from multiple datasets that were highly expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and associated with prognosis, and identified Mint3 as an important oncogene. Mint3 is implicated in controlling the malignant behaviours of pancreatic and breast cancer cells; however, our understanding of its role in HCC remains limited. Bioinformatic analysis of the underlying mechanisms showed that Mint3 may accelerate HCC development by suppressing cuproptosis. Cuproptosis, a novel copper-induced mode of cell death, may be associated with tumour progression. However, its involvement in tumourigenesis, metastasis, and patient prognosis requires further investigation. In this study, we aimed to identify novel biomarkers for HCC that may improve the prognosis of patients with HCC. We also investigated whether Mint3 regulated cuproptosis in HCC cells. Our results showed that Mint3 expression was frequently elevated in HCC specimens and was associated with increased tumour size, advanced tumour-node-metastasis stage, higher pathological grade, and poorer survival. Mint3 affected cell morphology and promoted proliferation, migration, and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition of HCC cells. Furthermore, our findings revealed that Mint3 overexpression resulted in reduced cuproptosis in HCC cells. The overexpression/down-regulation of FDX1, which is a critical mediator of cuproptosis, reversed Mint3 overexpression/downregulation-induced alterations of malignant phenotypes of HCC cells. Mechanistically, Mint3 exerted this effect via direct interaction with AHR, thus modulating the AHR signalling pathway and promoting AHR nuclear translocation. Further research demonstrated that AHR binds to the promoter region of FDX1 and subsequently inhibits it. Meanwhile, Mint3 knockdown suppressed HCC progression in patient-derived xenograft models. In the Mint3-knockout mouse group, Tp53 knockout/c-Myc overexpression treatment induced less spontaneous tumour formation than that in the WT group. Collectively, Mint3 is overexpressed in HCC and contributes to HCC progression by inhibiting cuproptosis via the AHR signalling pathway. Therefore, Mint3 may serve as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in HCC.

title: Vitamin D promotes endogenous sunscreen synthesis and ultraviolet protection in zebrafish
A new role of iridium(III) complexes in regulating pluripotency acquisition via mitochondrial remodulation
abstract: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hold great potential in regenerative medicine, disease modeling and cell biology studies. Reprogramming of mouse and human cells can be achieved through the introduction of transcription factors such as Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc (OSKM), or by chemical stimulation via exposure to small molecules. However, the role of ion compounds in reprogramming has remained relatively unexplored. Herein, we identify iridium (Ir)(III) complexes that enhance iPSC generation by promoting the perinuclear clustering of mitochondria. Mechanistically, Ir(III) complexes promote the nuclear localization of TCA cycle enzyme Pdha1 and increase the cellular acetyl-CoA, leading to chromatin remodeling at pluripotency genes by enhancing histones H3 and H4 acetylation. Our results reveal an important role for Ir(III) complexes in epigenetic regulation of cell fate and suggest a novel approach for iPSC generation.

title: Revealing the secrets of quorum sensing: a comprehensive review from signal mechanisms to practical applications
abstract: Quorum sensing (QS), a sophisticated cell-cell communication system in microorganisms, governs collective behaviors such as virulence, biofilm formation, and antibiotic resistance in a population-density-dependent manner. Targeting QS with quorum sensing inhibitors (QSIs) has emerged as a promising anti-virulence strategy to combat bacterial pathogens without exerting lethal selective pressure, thereby potentially curbing the rise of antimicrobial resistance. This review provides an integrated overview of the molecular mechanisms of QS signaling networks in Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, and extends the discussion to cross-kingdom communication and QS-like systems in fungi and bacteriophages. We systematically categorize QSIs based on their origins (plant, microbial, animal, and synthetic) and detail their mechanisms of action, focusing on the interference with autoinducer synthesis, degradation, receptor binding, and downstream signal transduction. Beyond a mere compilation of research advances, we critically evaluate the translational potential of QS interference, highlighting recent applications in clinical medicine (e.g., anti-biofilm coatings), agriculture (biocontrol agents), and environmental engineering (biofouling mitigation). Finally, we identify key challenges such as in vivo efficacy, ecological impact, and the translational gap, and propose future research priorities centered on smart delivery systems, narrow-spectrum inhibitors, and interdisciplinary collaboration. This comprehensive analysis underscores QS interference as a versatile and sustainable strategy, while charting a course for its evolution from a laboratory phenomenon to a practical solution.

title: The trade-off mechanism between fiber elongation and seed vigor formation mediated by the RCD1-MYC3 module in cotton
abstract: Cotton fiber length and seed vigor are crucial traits determining cotton farming efficiency and commercial value. Cotton fiber elongation and seed vigor establishment exhibit high spatiotemporal overlap and a close relationship. However, the underlying regulatory mechanisms orchestrating these two developmental processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identified an antagonistic module comprising radical-induced cell death 1 protein (GhRCD1) and transcription factor GhMYC3, which participates in this synergistic development. GhRCD1 positively regulated fiber elongation but negatively regulated seed vigor, whereas GhMYC3 had the opposite effects. Further studies demonstrated that GhRCD1 interacted with GhMYC3 through its RST domain, thereby attenuating GhMYC3-mediated promoter binding and transcriptional repression of GhGPX4, GhPER25, GhPER63, GhKCS12, GhCUT1, and GhFAD7A-1. In elongating fibers, higher GhRCD1 levels and lower GhMYC3 levels activate this module, which attenuates reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling and increases linolenic acid and very-long-chain fatty acid (VLCFA) levels, thereby promoting fiber elongation. In ripening seeds, lower GhRCD1 and higher GhMYC3 repress this module, which inhibits peroxidase (PER)-mediated ROS-cell wall demethylesterification-seed mechanical properties pathway, thus contributing to seed vigor formation. The genetic evidence further supported the GhMYC3 epistasis effect on GhRCD1 during fiber elongation and seed maturation coordination. Together, our findings elucidate a trade-off mechanism orchestrated by the antagonistic GhRCD1-GhMYC3 module, which coordinates cotton fiber elongation and seed vigor formation through their specific expression profiles and downstream regulatory networks in developing fibers and seeds. This study provides a basis for synergistic improvement of cottonseed and fiber quality.

title: Protein arginine methyltransferases as metabolic regulators: many roles beyond cancer
abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) comprises a cluster of interconnected metabolic abnormalities that collectively elevate the risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality. With its global prevalence escalating, understanding the molecular underpinnings of MetS has become increasingly imperative. Protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs), classically studied for their epigenetic functions and oncogenic properties, are now recognized as pivotal regulators of metabolic homeostasis. Emerging research reveals that these enzymes coordinate crucial aspects of cellular metabolism through multiple mechanisms, including methylation of metabolic transcription factors, modulation of nutrient-sensing pathways, and direct regulation of enzymatic activities in glucose and lipid metabolism. This review summarizes current knowledge on the metabolic roles of PRMTs, specifying their roles in the development and function of major metabolic tissues and their associations with various metabolic disorders. We further review how PRMTs influence metabolic processes by modifying key transcriptional networks and signaling cascades through methylation of different substrates. By integrating these insights, we establish PRMTs as central players in metabolic regulation and assess their potential as therapeutic targets for metabolic diseases beyond their established roles in cancer biology, thereby providing a framework for future research and clinical development.

title: Efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in female patients with cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed advanced cancer management by providing durable responses and significant survival benefits. However, sex-based differences in treatment outcomes remain poorly understood. In this systematic review and meta-analysis of 78 phase III randomized controlled trials including 56,332 patients, we specifically assessed the efficacy of ICIs in female patients. Overall, female patients experienced a overall survival (OS) benefit from immunotherapy (hazard ratio (HR)=0.80, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.76-0.84, P<0.0001), although considerable heterogeneity was observed across studies. Subgroup analyses showed no statistically significant differences in OS benefit across the examined stratification factors. Notably, we found female with squamous cell carcinoma did not demonstrate a statistically significant survival benefit from ICIs (HR=0.86, 95% CI: 0.71-1.04). Male patients demonstrated a more pronounced benefit (HR=0.77, 95% CI: 0.74-0.80, P<0.0001), although no improvement was noted in melanoma and glioblastoma. These findings highlight meaningful sex-based disparities in immunotherapy efficacy and underscore the need to integrate sex as a biological variable in clinical decision-making. Greater inclusion of women in clinical trials, identification of sex-specific biomarkers, and development of tailored strategies are essential to optimize immunotherapy outcomes and advance personalized cancer care.

title: Burden of cancer in China from 1990 to 2023 and projections to 2050
abstract: China bears one of the largest cancer burdens worldwide, yet comprehensive assessments integrating long-term age-sex patterns with uncertainty-aware projections based on the latest Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates remain limited. Using GBD 2023 data, we quantified trends in age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) for all malignant neoplasms in China from 1990 to 2023 and projected future trajectories through 2050. Period-specific changes were assessed using Joinpoint regression, and medium- to long-term projections were generated with a Bayesian age-period-cohort model incorporating uncertainty. Between 1990 and 2023, ASIR remained largely stable, with an average annual percent change (AAPC) of -0.02% per year, whereas ASMR declined substantially, with an AAPC of -1.55% per year. In 2023, ASIR and ASMR reached 2,259.08 and 114.02 per 100,000 population, respectively. Age-specific analyses demonstrated a steep increase in cancer burden with advancing age, characterized by higher incidence among middle-aged women and higher mortality among older men. Mortality trends exhibited distinct patterns, including an accelerated decline after 2008, a transient rebound during 2014-2017, and a modest upturn after 2020. Projections by the Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model indicate that ASIR is likely to rise modestly after a prolonged plateau-predominantly driven by women-while ASMR may gradually increase again after 2025, with greater uncertainty and rebound risk among men, particularly after 2040. These findings reveal an emerging structural divergence in China's cancer burden, with incidence increasingly concentrated in women and mortality in men. This pattern highlights the need for sex- and age-specific cancer control strategies, including strengthened risk-factor control and multimorbidity management in men, high-quality screening and survivorship care in women, and continuous surveillance to recalibrate policies as observed trends deviate from projected trajectories.

title: A sesterterpenoid derivative alleviates ulcerative colitis through targeting ProRS to suppress the NLRP3 inflammasome
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a prevalent inflammatory bowel disease that affects millions of people worldwide, for which no definitive cure currently exists. Herein, we report the discovery of a novel sesterterpenoid derivative, ColD14, with a complicated cage-like structure and contiguous stereogenic centers, which exhibits significant anti-NLRP3 inflammasome activity. Proteomic and biochemical studies identified glutamyl-prolyl tRNA synthetase (EPRS) as a direct target of ColD14. Both EPRS knockdown and pharmacological inhibition by ColD14 reduced NLRP3 inflammasome activation, underscoring the crucial role of EPRS in inflammatory processes. Mechanistically, through the molecular interaction with amino acid residues R1152, E1154, and R1278 at the ATP site, ColD14 inhibited prolyl-tRNA synthetase (ProRS) activity. This suppression triggered the amino acid response (AAR) pathway and consequently attenuated NLRP3 inflammasome activation via mitophagy regulation. In vivo, ColD14 activated the AAR signaling pathway, triggered mitophagy, and inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation, thereby alleviating DSS-induced colitis in mice. Taken together, our findings underscored the significance of EPRS in NLRP3 inflammasome activation and suggested that the EPRS inhibitor, ColD14, may be valuable in ulcerative colitis therapy via the EPRS-AAR-mitophagy axis.

title: An innovative model for integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine: state-target differentiation and treatment
abstract: Facing the health challenges posed by global population aging and the increasing burden of chronic non-communicable diseases, Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine (ITCWM) in China has achieved notable progress over the past 70 years. However, the traditional "combination of disease and syndrome" model exhibits several limitations, including the disconnect between syndrome differentiation and disease stages, insufficient precision in the targeting of Chinese herbal medicines, inconsistencies in disease nomenclature between Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and Western Medicine (WM), and fragmentation in diagnosis and treatment. The "state-target differentiation and treatment" (STDT) model, proposed in 2015, enables the organic integration of TCM's macroscopic state modulation and WM's microscopic targeting. Under the guidance of this theory, Tong Xiaolin classified diabetes into four stages: stagnation, heat, deficiency, and injury. This classification has been incorporated into the International Guideline for Diagnostic and Treatment Principles of Chinese Medicine in Diabetes, issued by the World Federation of Chinese Medicine Societies. By reconstructing the diagnostic and treatment system of ITCWM, reconstructing a modern system for Chinese herbal medicine, and promoting alignment between TCM and WM disease spectra, this approach facilitates the transformation of TCM from experience-based medicine to precision medicine. It also advances the internationalization of TCM and provides a "Chinese solution" for the development of ITCWM and global health governance.

title: Before the heat shock response: who guards the plasma membrane?

Intraputaminal AAV9 co-delivery of AADC and GDNF in severe AADC deficiency: first-in-human pediatric dose-escalation study
abstract: Aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) deficiency is a rare, severe inherited neurotransmitter disorder causing combined monoamine depletion and severe motor, autonomic, and developmental impairment. Building on established intraputaminal AAV-mediated AADC replacement, we evaluated a next-generation dual-mechanism strategy that couples restoration of dopamine synthesis with neurotrophic circuit support by delivering an AAV9 vector co-expressing human AADC and glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) in children with genetically confirmed severe AADC deficiency. Four children (36-59 months; 1 female, 3 males) without head control at baseline received a single bilateral MRI-guided intraputaminal infusion at one of three dose levels (2.0×10 11 , 6.0×10 11 , or 1.28×10 12 vector genomes) and were followed for 52 weeks. The primary endpoint was safety and tolerability. Key secondary outcomes assessed cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) monoamine metabolites, 18 F-DOPA PET, motor development, and disease-related symptoms. Treatment was feasible and generally well tolerated, with no vector-related serious adverse events. Biomarker analyses provided convergent evidence of target engagement, including increased CSF metabolites and improved 18 F-DOPA uptake, accompanied by improvements in motor function and symptom burden in most participants. By Week 52, one participant achieved full head control and independent sitting, and two achieved partial head control. These first-in-human findings support a dual-gene "enzyme restoration plus circuit support" paradigm and provide a strong translational rationale for further clinical development of this next-generation gene therapy for severe AADC deficiency. ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05765981.

title: A gustatory receptor mediates sucrose detection to enhance moth reproductive fitness
abstract: The mutualism between pollinators and flowering plants is a fundamental interaction in ecosystems, mediated by nectar rewards. Sucrose, a major component of floral nectar, is a key driver of pollinator foraging, yet the sensory mechanisms underlying sucrose detection are poorly defined. Here we demonstrate that the pollinator Mythimna separata exhibits a strong sex-independent preference for sucrose, which directly enhances reproductive fitness. We identify MsepGR5, a gustatory receptor expressed in antennal sensilla chaetica, as a key receptor mediating sucrose detection. Crucially, genetic ablation of MsepGR5 completely abolishes both sucrose-evoked neural responses and feeding behavior. Our findings uncover a dedicated gustatory pathway for sucrose detection and establish its critical role in reproductive success in M. separata.

title: Neoadjuvant therapy reshapes the therapeutic value of distal lymphadenectomy in cT3/4a proximal gastric cancer

A CDC20 allelic series reveals stage-specific control of metaphase-to-anaphase transitions during mitosis and meiosis in rice
abstract: The metaphase-to-anaphase transition is a critically controlled checkpoint essential for precise chromosome segregation. In yeast and animals, cell division cycle 20 (CDC20) serves as an essential coactivator of the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C), triggering the degradation of key substrates to initiate anaphase. Plants, however, often possess multiple CDC20 homologs, whose functional specificity remains poorly characterized. Employing CRISPR/Cas9 technology, we generated a series of cdc20 triple mutants in rice (Oryza sativa) and performed a systematic cytological analysis to investigate the functions of all three CDC20 genes. Complete loss of CDC20s' function resulted in gametophytic mitotic defects, ultimately causing bilateral gametophyte lethality. We obtained hypomorphic alleles specifically displaying disrupted meiosis without mitotic defects. The cdc20-triple-1 and cdc20-triple-2 mutants were arrested at metaphase I with normal chromosome alignment, but failed to remove sister chromatid cohesin 3 (SCC3) from chromosome arms. In contrast, the cdc20-triple-3 and cdc20-triple-4 alleles progressed through meiosis I but arrested at metaphase II, exhibiting aberrant spindles and chromosome missegregation. We further demonstrated that CDC20s regulated shugoshin 1 (SGO1) distributive pattern: SGO1 loaded normally in cdc20-triple-1 but persisted at centromeres and failed to detach, even when sister chromatids separated aberrantly. However, cdc20-triple-3 mutants showed normal SGO1 unloading, suggesting that timely SGO1 removal from centromeres depends on a CDC20-mediated metaphase I-to-anaphase I transition. Our findings reveal that rice CDC20 homologs play a critical role in controlling the metaphase-to-anaphase transition throughout both mitosis and meiosis, thereby ensuring tight regulation and enhancing genomic stability during sexual reproduction.

title: Treatment of hypoplastic aortic arch with Stanford type B aortic dissection using “double arch” technique with thoracic endovascular aortic repair

SYVN1-mediated succinate accumulation exacerbates heart failure
abstract: Metabolic remodeling, defined as changes in the energy substrate preferences and energy production efficiency of the myocardium, is one of the pathogenic characteristics of failing hearts, though its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Through untargeted metabolomics coupled with targeted mass spectrometry, we report that plasma succinate levels are significantly elevated in patients with impaired cardiac function (ejection fraction, EF<50%) compared to those with preserved EF (EF⩾50%). Succinate is a key metabolite intermediate in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that β-adrenergic receptor activation upregulates synoviolin 1 (SYVN1), which promotes the ubiquitination and degradation of nuclear respiratory factor 1 (NRF1). In turn, this downregulates the expression of succinate dehydrogenase complex iron sulfur subunit B (SDHB), leading to intracellular succinate accumulation and subsequent release. Furthermore, we show that the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor empagliflozin binds to NRF1, restores SDHB expression, normalizes succinate levels, and ameliorates cardiac dysfunction in a pressure-overload model. Our findings delineate a novel SYVN1/NRF1/SDHB-succinate axis that drives mitochondrial dysfunction in heart failure, and identify its potential as a therapeutic target for metabolic modulation.

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveal developmental dynamics of the human cerebral cortex and striatum
abstract: The human fetal brain undergoes morphological changes that contribute to the development of regional functionalities. However, the features of structural development, the underlying molecular and cellular signatures in the fetal brain, remain unclear. With spatial transcriptomics and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), we identified 25 forebrain regions and characterized the dynamic changes in the cortex and striatum during the late first and early second trimesters. In particular, we discovered that the temporal lobe enriched NPY-expressing L2/3 excitatory (EX) neurons potentially interacted with L4 EX neurons during cortical expansion and arealization. Additionally, the gyrus and sulcus were developmentally asynchronous, in which HOPX and SPARC genes were potentially involved. Further investigation on the striatum showed specific genes and cell types that were enriched in patch and matrix compartments, and SST-positive interneurons potentially involved in the development of these structures. Together, our results give insights into the understanding of early fetal brain development.

title: New perspectives on plant water sensing
Machine learning-driven discovery and longitudinal validation of eGDR and TyG-BMI for stratifying risk in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome
Structural basis of nucleotide-dependent conformational switching of a CBS-family protein on the archaeal 50S ribosome
abstract: Ribosome, the universally conserved cellular machinery, orchestrates protein synthesis across all organisms. Ribosome-associated factors that regulate translation during biogenesis and stress adaptation remain underexplored in archaea due to limited structural data. Here we present eight cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of the archaeal 50S ribosomal subunit at resolutions of 2.07-3.26 Å, revealing a previously uncharacterized cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) domain-containing protein positioned above the peptidyl transferase center, with an extended loop that inserts deeply into the peptide exit tunnel. Intriguingly, distinct adenosine derivatives occupy the ligand-binding pocket of the CBS protein in different structural states of the 50S subunit. Molecular dynamics simulations indicate that ATP binding induces a more contracted conformation of the extended loop, suggesting that nucleotide occupancy may modulate this protein's ribosome-association mode. Biochemical and bioinformatic analyses reveal that the extended loop is predominantly found in archaea, suggesting lineage-specific adaptations of ribosome-associated CBS proteins. Furthermore, the relatively sparse and dispersed distribution of rRNA modifications likely reflects organism-specific adaptations. Collectively, this work provides a structural framework for understanding how CBS-family proteins engage the archaeal ribosome and how their association may be tuned by cellular nucleotide status, offering insights into the molecular diversity of ribosome-associated factors and their roles in stress adaptation.

title: Inflammation as a central driver in AML pathogenesis and therapy resistance
abstract: Inflammation is a prominent feature of the bone marrow microenvironment in acute myeloid leukemia and contributes to leukemic evolution, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Accumulating evidence indicates that inflammatory signals in AML arise from multiple sources, including age-associated inflammaging, mutation-driven pathways, cell-intrinsic stress programs, and external inflammatory stimuli such as infections. These signals collectively facilitate the progression from clonal hematopoiesis and other pre-leukemic states to overt leukemia and support malignant expansion. Leukemic blasts, immune effector and regulatory cells, mesenchymal stromal cells, and endothelial cells collectively establish an inflammatory niche through the production of cytokines and chemokines. This niche supports leukemic stem cell maintenance and fitness, promotes metabolic adaptation and survival, and disrupts normal hematopoiesis and immune surveillance. The inflammatory microenvironment can also compromise therapeutic efficacy by inducing drug tolerance, reinforcing protective bone marrow niches, and reshaping responses to chemotherapy, targeted therapies, immunotherapies, and transplantation-associated graft-versus-leukemia effects. Although increasing mechanistic insights have inspired strategies aimed at neutralizing inflammatory mediators, blocking downstream signaling pathways, or reprogramming the microenvironment to restore anti-leukemic immunity, such anti-inflammatory approaches remain incompletely explored in clinical practice. A deeper understanding of cell type-specific inflammatory circuits and cytokine interactions will be essential for developing rational combination therapies to overcome microenvironment-driven resistance.

β2-adrenergic receptor agonist regulates macrophage polarization via HMGB1 in immune thrombocytopenia
abstract: An imbalance in M1/M2 polarization is linked to the pathogenesis of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). Terbutaline, a β2-adrenergic receptor agonist, can significantly increase the percentage of Tregs, attenuating thrombocytopenia in ITP. The effect of terbutaline on M1/M2 polarization in ITP remains uncertain. This study aimed to elucidate the connection between splenic sympathetic nerves and macrophage polarization and to assess the effect of terbutaline on macrophages in ITP. Peripheral blood-derived CD14 + monocytes were isolated from ITP patients and healthy donors and cultured in vitro. Spleen-derived macrophages were isolated from murine ITP models. Flow cytometry was used to analyze the percentages of M1 and M2 macrophages, assess the expression of macrophage markers, and perform in vitro phagocytosis assays. Targeted and nontargeted quantitative metabolomic analyses of amino acids in macrophages were conducted. Passive ITP models were used to examine the therapeutic benefits of terbutaline and its ability to modulate macrophage polarization. Decreased sympathetic nerve fibers and an imbalance in macrophage polarization were observed in the spleens of ITP mice. Sympathectomy aggravated the imbalance of splenic macrophage polarization and decreased platelet counts in mice. Recombinant high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) offset the altered polarization and platelet phagocytosis by splenic macrophages from ITP mice induced by terbutaline. Terbutaline alleviated the abnormal polarization of macrophages from patients with ITP. Terbutaline increased platelet counts in passive ITP murine models. Our study preliminarily suggests that terbutaline has the potential to alter abnormal macrophage polarization and reduce platelet phagocytosis and that HMGB1 could be involved in the mechanism of ITP.

title: Optimization of lipid nanoparticles reduces hepatic accumulation and enhances local delivery of mRNA
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the most widely used non-viral gene delivery system, particularly for mRNA therapeutics. However, predominant hepatic accumulation and poor local delivery remain major barriers to their broader application. To address this challenge, we employed a design of experiments (DOE) strategy to systematically refine LNP composition and identified an optimized formulation, SM102M. Compared with the parental SM102 formulation, SM102M markedly reduced liver-associated signal after both intramuscular and intravenous administration, while preserving or enhancing local expression after local delivery. Across multiple local administration routes, including intramuscular, intracerebroventricular, and intravitreal injection, SM102M supported localized gene delivery and gene editing with minimal liver-associated signal. Mechanistically, the altered biodistribution of SM102M was associated with reduced apolipoprotein E (ApoE) binding, lower systemic exposure, and diminished lysosomal escape in hepatocytes. SM102M also showed favorable tolerability and maintained local delivery performance under repeated administration. Together, these findings establish DOE as a practical framework for rational LNP engineering and identify a formulation with reduced hepatic reporter expression and improved local delivery performance.

title: Effects of Ulva prolifera polysaccharide calcium on flavor compound deposition, myofiber conversion and gut microbiota profiles in broilers
abstract: Ulva prolifera polysaccharide (UPP), a bioactive compound derived from marine algae, exhibits potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and lipid-regulatory activities. However, the mechanism by which its calcium chelate form (UPP-Ca) affects muscle development remains largely unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the patterns of flavor compound deposition and muscle fiber composition across different muscle regions in broilers at different developmental stages and to determine the effects of UPP-Ca (200, 400, and 800 mg/kg) and UPP on meat quality and gut microbiota in vivo (1-day-old yellow-feathered broilers) or in vitro (C2C12 myoblasts). We found that flavor fatty acids were gradually deposited with age, and unsaturated fatty acids and slow-type muscle fibers were mainly accumulated in the thigh muscle of broilers. Dietary supplementation with 200 mg/kg UPP and UPP-Ca improved final body weight, average daily gain, and muscle redness; however, these benefits were weakened at higher UPP-Ca doses (400 and 800 mg/kg). Both 200 mg/kg UPP and UPP-Ca selectively promoted and optimized the contents of favorable flavor-related amino acids and polyunsaturated fatty acids at 28 or 70 d. However, only 200 mg/kg UPP-Ca increased C20:4n6 and C20:5n3 in thigh muscle, along with serine content and the PUFAs/SFA ratio in breast muscle. Furthermore, 200 mg/kg UPP-Ca enhanced the expression of MYH1B, MYH1E, MYH7, MyOD, and Myf5 in thigh and breast muscle, and this was also confirmed by in vitro experiments, showing that UPP-Ca promoted myoblast proliferation and lipid metabolism and also modulated myofiber differentiation and conversion towards type I. Additionally, 200 mg/kg UPP-Ca administration reshaped gut microbiota profiles at 28 d, with a significant rise in the Rikenellaceae_RC9_gut_group and Subdoligramilum in intestinal chyme, which were significantly associated with flavor substrates and muscle fiber types. Collectively, these results indicate that 200 mg/kg UPP-Ca improves growth performance and meat quality by selectively promoting flavor compound deposition and myofiber type conversion in muscle of broilers, while modulating beneficial gut microbiota profiles at an early age.

title: Targeting CDK2 ameliorates allergic asthma through suppression of epithelial chemokine production and T cell inflammatory responses
abstract: Allergic asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease driven by dysregulated type 2 immunity and aberrant epithelial-immune crosstalk. Despite advances in biologic therapies, many patients remain refractory to current treatments, underscoring the need for novel strategies that simultaneously target multiple pathogenic axes. Here, we show that cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) is upregulated in bronchoalveolar lavage cells from asthmatic patients and its expression correlates with enhanced cell cycle activity, inflammatory signatures, and T cell activation in bronchial epithelium across six independent cohorts. In an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced murine model, pharmacological inhibition with a highly selective small-molecule CDK2 inhibitor (CDK2i) markedly alleviated airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR), eosinophilic inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and peribronchial fibrosis, with effects comparable to those of dexamethasone. Mechanistically, CDK2i suppressed chemokine production in airway epithelial cells, thereby reducing T cell recruitment, while concurrently inducing G1/S cell-cycle arrest in T lymphocytes and blunting their production of Th2 cytokines. Integrated transcriptomic and functional analyses suggested that CDK2 may be involved in two pathways: epithelial-driven immune cell trafficking and T cell clonal expansion. Together, these findings suggest that selective CDK2 inhibition represents a promising experimental strategy for attenuating allergic airway inflammation and warrants further investigation in preclinical models of asthma.

title: Circulating cell-free Epstein-Barr virus DNA measurement for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: advancing towards ctDNA-guided, risk-adaptive individualized treatment
abstract: Circulating tumor-derived DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a pivotal tool for cancer screening, pre-treatment prognostic risk stratification, on-treatment response evaluation, and post-treatment recurrence surveillance. The pursuit of tumor-specific ctDNA biomarkers has been a long-standing and concerted effort in cancer research. Among these, cell-free Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA (cfEBV DNA) has been recognized as a robust disease-specific biomarker for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) in endemic regions. EBV was the first DNA virus linked to human malignancies and is predominantly present in its latent form in NPC. For patients with NPC, cfEBV DNA released by dead tumor cells not only reflects tumor burden but is also associated with the host immune status and viral clearance capacity. More importantly, external stressors such as chemotherapy and radiotherapy can alter the infection status of EBV from latency to lytic phase, which may lead to increased viral DNA synthesis, as well as the expression of lytic-associated proteins. These treatment-induced changes can, in turn, impact the therapeutic efficacy of NPC. Owing to these unique properties, cfEBV DNA emerges as a promising biomarker for the longitudinal assessment of therapeutic response and clinical outcomes in NPC. This review summarizes recent advances in the application of cfEBV DNA for disease screening, prognostication, and surveillance, with particular emphasis on its serial tracing during treatment for real-time response evaluation and dynamic recurrence risk monitoring. We also discuss future perspectives on risk-adaptive, individualized treatment strategies of NPC guided by longitudinal cfEBV DNA monitoring during treatment.

title: Current understanding and new promises of umbilical cord blood in emerging clinical applications
abstract: Umbilical cord blood (UCB) has become an important resource for regenerative medicine owing to its unique cellular composition, immune immaturity, and abundance of bioactive factors. Although UCB was initially applied in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, accumulating evidence indicates that its diverse cellular and paracrine components possess broad regenerative potential. Beyond conventional hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, substantial progress has expanded the therapeutic scope of UCB to immune cell-based therapies, the treatment of genetic and metabolic disorders, and tissue repair. In this review, we focus on the biological characteristics of the key cellular and noncellular components of UCB and analyze how these properties support tissue repair, immunomodulation, and regeneration across multiple organ systems. We further summarize recent technological advances, including cell engineering, gene modification, and manufacturing technologies, that have enhanced the scalability and therapeutic potential of UCB-derived products. In addition, we highlight current challenges that limit their widespread clinical application. This review aims to provide a framework for optimizing UCB-based therapies and accelerating their clinical translation. Optimizing UCB collection, processing, and application strategies may further unlock its therapeutic potential, thereby improving clinical efficacy and expanding its applicability to a broader range of diseases.

title: BHLHE40 as a transcriptional rheostat: decoding microenvironmental signals in context-dependent tumor plasticity
abstract: The basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor BHLHE40 (also known as BHLHB2, DEC1, STRA13) functions as a critical molecular rheostat in cancer biology, exhibiting context-dependent roles that contribute to tumor plasticity. This review synthesizes current knowledge of BHLHE40, with emphasis on its structural features, including DNA binding, dimerization, and regulatory domains, as well as its integration of key physiological signals, such as circadian rhythm regulation, hypoxic adaptation, cellular senescence, and immune modulation. Pancancer analyses indicate that BHLHE40 expression is dysregulated across multiple tumor types. Elevated expression is associated with poor prognosis in cancers such as glioblastoma, acute myeloid leukemia, and ovarian cancer, whereas it correlates with favorable outcomes in breast and kidney cancers. Notably, the functional role of BHLHE40 is highly tissue-dependent. It promotes tumor progression in hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by enhancing proliferation, invasion, migration, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and therapeutic resistance. In contrast, BHLHE40 exhibits tumor-suppressive effects in prostate cancer by inducing cellular senescence, and in endometrial cancer by inhibiting EMT. The tumor microenvironment plays a pivotal role in modulating BHLHE40 activity, with factors such as hypoxia, cytokine signaling, and immune cell interactions shaping its oncogenic or tumor-suppressive functions. Importantly, its role in maintaining CD8 + T-cell effector function during immune checkpoint blockade highlights its therapeutic potential. However, the context-dependent duality of BHLHE40 presents significant challenges for clinical targeting. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including targeted protein degradation approaches and advanced tumor models such as patient-derived organoids, offer promising avenues for intervention. Future studies integrating multi-omics data and spatial transcriptomics will be essential to fully elucidate the role of BHLHE40 and to harness its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune evasion.

title: DESIGN: a framework for generative AI-enabled crop molecular design-driven breeding
abstract: Crop breeding is shifting from selecting naturally occurring variants to actively designing genetic features. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) provides a computational foundation for this transition; however, its application in crop systems remains limited. This review bridges this gap by systematically evaluating the translational potential of GenAI for crop molecular design breeding. We examine four major computational architectures and their applications across six key areas relevant to crop breeding: gene regulatory element design, protein engineering, small-molecule generation, gene-editing tool optimization, single-cell modeling, and cross-domain knowledge integration. Building on these advances, we propose the DESIGN framework, which organizes GenAI-enabled breeding into six synergistic capabilities: Discover, Engineer, Simulate, Integrate, Generate, and Navigate, thereby forming a closed-loop system spanning molecular design to field deployment. Finally, we discuss key bottlenecks in data, models, and validation, and outline a roadmap for translating GenAI into breeding practice. This review provides a conceptual and methodological foundation for the emerging paradigm of design-driven crop breeding.

title: pH-responsive biomimetic liposomes enhance targeted immunotherapy of bladder cancer
abstract: Bladder cancer is one of the most prevalent malignant tumors of the urinary system, and its high incidence and mortality seriously threaten human health. Although emerging immunotherapies have achieved remarkable results in bladder cancer, they still face great challenges such as immune tolerance and low response rates in clinical practice. Therefore, to overcome immunotherapy resistance and low response rates, we designed and prepared a pH-responsive biomimetic liposome (LP) encapsulating the lymphocyte activation gene 3 protein (FGFR) inhibitor erdafitinib using the thin-film hydration method, yielding erdafitinib-loaded liposomes (ELPs). Meanwhile, bladder cancer cell membranes (M) were hybridized onto the liposomal surface to construct biomimetic liposomes (MELPs), thereby endowing the liposomes with homologous tumor-targeting capability through membrane-mediated recognition. The study demonstrated that MELP could directly target the FGFR receptor to trigger ferroptosis in bladder cancer cells through the JAK2-STAT3-GPX4 signaling pathway, as well as promote macrophage polarization and dendritic cell maturation in vitro, thereby stimulating antitumor immune responses. MELP exhibited good biosafety and bladder tumor-targeting ability based on biodistribution in vivo. Moreover, MELP combined with the LAG-3 antibody not only effectively inhibited bladder tumor growth and metastasis but also remodeled the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting dendritic cell maturation, enhancing CD8 + T lymphocyte infiltration, and inducing M1-type macrophage polarization in bladder tumors, which can convert immunologically "cold" tumors into "hot" tumors, thereby potentiating the therapeutic efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade and significantly prolonging survival. Therefore, the combination of MELP and LAG-3 antibody can effectively enhance targeted immunotherapy against bladder tumors, which can also provide a novel strategy for bladder cancer.

title: Emerging biotechnological approaches in alcoholic liver disease: natural compounds, delivery systems, and translational potential
abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD), resulting from chronic and excessive alcohol consumption, remains a major global public health burden. However, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely elucidated, and there are no specific biomarkers or effective pharmacological therapies currently available. Clinically, ALD diagnosis largely relies on patients' self-reported drinking history and nonspecific biochemical or imaging findings, which limits accurate detection and targeted treatment. Consequently, there is an urgent need for safe, accessible, and effective preventive strategies to alleviate ALD progression. Recent studies have demonstrated that dietary regulation and food-derived bioactive compounds-such as polyphenols, probiotics, and fatty acids-can effectively attenuate alcohol-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and gut-liver axis dysfunction. This review systematically summarizes recent advances (2020-2025) in the study of dietary bioactive compounds with protective roles against ALD, focusing on their molecular mechanisms, including antioxidative, anti-inflammatory, and microbiota-modulating effects. Furthermore, the paper highlights biotechnological innovations in enhancing the efficacy of bioactive compounds, such as advanced delivery systems, processing technologies, and functional food design, which improve the stability, bioavailability, and targeted efficacy of these compounds. Accumulating evidence supports the translational potential of nutrition-based interventions in preventing and managing ALD. However, significant challenges remain, including inter-individual variability, safety validation, and regulatory acceptance. Looking forward, precision nutrition, next-generation probiotics (NGPs), intelligent delivery systems, AI-driven formulation design, and sustainable food sources are expected to drive innovation in ALD prevention. Overall, this review aims to provide a timely and comprehensive overview of emerging nutrition-based strategies, offering valuable insights for developing scientific, practical, and health-promoting nutritional interventions against ALD.

title: Awakening cryptic C1 metabolism: engineering de novo formatotrophy in Yarrowia lipolytica unlocks one-carbon biomanufacturing potential
ATF6α mediates Cr(VI)-induced acute hepatotoxicity via GRP78-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction under oxidative stress
abstract: Acute exposure to the common environmental toxin, hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)), can cause severe chemical hepatotoxicity. Although endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is closely associated with Cr(VI)-induced liver damage, the underlying mechanism requires further investigation. In this study, mice and hepatocytes exposed to Cr(VI) were used to analyze the effects of reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated ER stress on acute liver injury, with a particular focus on the activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6) branch. It was found that Cr(VI) stimulated the expression and cleavage of ATF6α, while the level of ATF6β was decreased. Pharmacological inhibition and gene knockdown of ATF6α alleviated liver damage caused by Cr(VI). Mechanistically, cleaved ATF6α translocated to the nucleus and directly bound to the promoter of HSPA5 to induce GRP78 transcription, which was closely related to mitochondrial impairment. HSPA5 interference in Cr(VI)-exposed hepatocytes partially improved mitochondrial homeostasis and mitochondria-dependent apoptosis. Interestingly, suppression of ATF6β increased site 1 protease (S1P) but not site 2 protease (S2P), promoting ATF6α cleavage in the Golgi apparatus. Overall, these findings establish ATF6α as a key regulator of Cr(VI)-induced hepatotoxicity via GRP78-mediated mitochondrial dysfunction under oxidative ER stress, suggesting the therapeutic potential of targeting the ATF6 pathway in xenobiotic-induced hepatic injury.

title: Rethinking incomplete immune reconstitution in people living with HIV: beyond CD4 metrics toward multi-omics guided precision care
Epigenetics in development, disease, and therapy: from mechanisms to clinical interventions
abstract: Epigenetics, defined as the regulatory mechanisms that modulate genetic information flow without altering the DNA sequence, plays a crucial role in development, aging, and disease. This review explores the key epigenetic mechanisms-DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin remodeling, and non-coding RNAs-and their contributions to cellular differentiation, tissue homeostasis, and disease progression. We focus on their roles in gametogenesis, early development, stem cell reprogramming, and aging, highlighting how epigenetic alterations influence health and disease. The review also discusses emerging therapeutic approaches targeting epigenetic modifications, with potential applications in disease treatment and longevity. Finally, we examine the future of epigenetic research, emphasizing the need for precision therapies and the integration of epigenetic tools in clinical practice.

title: Weaning stress reprograms immune translation through GC biased codon usage in piglets with gut microbiota dysbiosis
abstract: Weaning stress constitutes a critical early-life challenge that disrupts immune homeostasis and reshapes gut microbiota composition. Here, we integrate ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) to characterize transcriptional and translational responses in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy and weaning piglets. We show that weaning stress induces widespread translational reprogramming, with pronounced effects on immune genes, including significantly increased translation efficiency of key inflammatory mediators CD82, CCL25, and TNFSF13. These changes are accompanied by distinct shifts in codon usage patterns, with genes exhibiting enhanced translation in the weaning group displaying enrichment of GC-ending codons (GC3), including those encoding leucine, glutamate, and lysine. Integrative analysis further suggests a coordinated relationship between translational remodeling and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Genera enriched in healthy piglets, including Romboutsia, Lactobacillus, and Turicibacter, were associated with AT-rich codon usage patterns, whereas genera expanded under weaning stress, such as Fusobacterium and Streptococcus, were linked to GC-enriched codon profiles, concomitant with increased GC3 content and codon adaptation index. Collectively, these findings identify a previously unrecognized association between microbiota composition and codon-usage-linked translational regulation during stress-induced immune responses, providing a framework for understanding microbiome-host interactions at the level of translational control.

title: MdRAD5B regulates the chromatin accessibility of MdMYB14 under cold by associating with a transcription factor MdLSD1
abstract: RADIATION SENSITIVE 5B (MdRAD5B) has previously been identified as a chromatin remodeler involved in regulating the chromatin accessibility and H3K27me3 modification of genes. However, how RAD5B regulates the chromatin accessibility of target genes remains largely unclear. Here, we find that MdRAD5B positively regulates apple cold tolerance by modulating the expression of cold-responsive genes. Under cold stress, MdRAD5B regulates the expression of cold-responsive genes, including MdMYB14, through its chromatin remodeling function. Further study reveals that the transcription factor LESION SIMULATING DISEASE 1 (MdLSD1) recruits MdRAD5B and reduces the chromatin accessibility of MdMYB14. MdMYB14, a downstream target of MdLSD1 and a negative regulator of cold tolerance, binds to the promoter region of MdCBF3 and inhibits its expression. Additionally, we identified a natural variation, a non-synonymous mutation at position 1,780 of the RAD5B CDS (RAD5B CDS1780 ), which affects apple cold tolerance by altering the ATPase activity of RAD5B. Taken together, our results unravel the underlying molecular mechanism by which MdRAD5B negatively regulates the chromatin accessibility of MdMYB14 through MdLSD1 in apple responses to cold.

title: Polysocial risk score predicts chronic kidney disease incidence and prognosis: mechanistic insights from plasma metabolome, proteome and lifestyle
abstract: The cumulative impact of multiple social determinants of health (SDHs) on chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains poorly understood. This prospective study examined the association of a polysocial risk score (PsRS) with CKD incidence and subsequent risks of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, and explored potential mediating pathways via multi-omics profiling and lifestyle factors. We analyzed 279,548 participants free of CKD at baseline and 19,761 patients with established CKD in the UK Biobank. The PsRS integrated 15 factors across economic, educational, healthcare, neighborhood, and social domains. Plasma metabolomic and proteomic profiles were analyzed to identify omics signatures associated with the PsRS. An unhealthy lifestyle score (uHLS) was derived based on body mass index, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, sleep, and diet. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between the PsRS and outcomes. Mediation analyses were performed in subsets with available omics and lifestyle data. Over a median follow-up of 13 years, 6,628 incident CKD cases, 3,724 CVD events, and 2,486 deaths were documented. The PsRS demonstrated a positive association with incident CKD risk among CKD-free participants (per 1-point increase: HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.11-1.14), as well as with CVD (HR=1.08; 95% CI: 1.07-1.10) and all-cause mortality (HR=1.12; 95% CI: 1.10-1.14) in CKD patients. The PsRS significantly improved the predictive performance of conventional clinical models across all outcomes, as indicated by increases in the C-index, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Multi-omics analyses revealed a PsRS-associated metabolomic signature (94 metabolites primarily involved in amino acids, fatty acids, and lipoproteins) and a proteomic signature (428 proteins primarily involved in immune/inflammatory responses, cellular signaling, and fibrosis). These omics signatures mediated substantial proportions of the PsRS-outcome associations (metabolomic: 16.64%-27.09%; proteomic: 53.09%-85.21%), as did the uHLS (8.26%-12.51%). In conclusion, the PsRS effectively predicts CKD development and prognosis, largely mediated through metabolomic and proteomic pathways.

title: Tooth organoids: bridging developmental biology and regenerative dentistry
Disrupted early molar patterning in syngnathia mouse model
abstract: It is well established that tooth morphogenesis initiates at embryonic day 11.5 (E11.5), characterized by the specification of a single molar germ in each jaw quadrant. However, the developmental mechanisms establishing the spatially distinct maxillary and mandibular identities along the jaw axis prior to this stage remain elusive. In Wnt1-Cre;pMes-Bmp4 transgenic mice, a pathological model recapitulating human syngnathia (resulting in bilateral jaw fusion), we demonstrate here that BMP4 overexpression in cranial neural crest cells (CNCC) disrupts early molar patterning with 100% penetrance, manifesting as the formation of only one molar germ within each unilateral fused jaw structure, establishing this model as a valuable tool for investigating the patterning of maxillary and mandibular molar germs during jaw development. Systematic analysis of wild-type embryos revealed the emergence of a single molar primordium in the unilateral first pharyngeal arch (PA1) by E9.0. This primordium undergoes segregation to form the maxillary and mandibular molar germs between E9.5 and E9.75, a process synchronized with the anteroposterior patterning of PA1. Comparative studies with the mutant model indicated that this developmental segregation depends on coordinated migration of CNCC-derived molar primordium and a BMP4/FGF8-dependent gene regulatory network (GRN) at the maxillomandibular junction. Pathologically elevated BMP4 signaling upregulates the p38 intracellular pathway in the mutant jaws, perturbing the finely tuned GRN and disrupting post-migratory CNCC migration. These perturbations collectively lead to defective molar segregation in the syngnathia mouse model. Our findings elucidate fundamental mechanisms governing early molar patterning and may provide molecular explanations for syngnathia-associated molar oligodontia in humans.

title: A ketamine derivative exerts enhanced antidepressant effects via adenosine signaling
abstract: Ketamine exerts rapid antidepressant effects but is limited by dissociative and abuse-related side effects, highlighting the need for safer alternatives. Here, we identify 3C-DCK, a rationally designed ketamine derivative, through adenosine dynamics in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). Using the GRAB Ado1.0 sensor, we show that 3C-DCK elicits more potent and sustained extracellular adenosine release than ketamine at lower doses. Mechanistically, 3C-DCK lowers the intracellular ATP/ADP ratio, thereby driving equilibrative nucleoside transporter (ENT)-dependent adenosine efflux without inducing neuronal hyperexcitation or extracellular ATP hydrolysis. In chronically stressed mice, a single 2 mg/kg dose produced rapid and durable antidepressant-like effects lasting up to 72 h, exceeding the duration of ketamine. These effects required A1 and A2A receptor signalling and occurred without hyperlocomotion or ataxia. Together, our findings establish adenosine signaling as a druggable axis for dissociating therapeutic efficacy from ketamine-associated adverse effects and provide a framework for the development of next-generation rapid-acting antidepressants.

title: PRDM16 attenuates pulmonary fibrosis through NuRD-mediated epigenetic remodeling in lung fibroblasts
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive, and fatal fibrotic lung disease with a poor prognosis. While epigenetic regulation is increasingly recognized as a key driver of fibrogenesis, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unclear. In this study, we identify PR domain-containing protein 16 (PRDM16) as a critical epigenetic repressor of profibrotic gene transcription. PRDM16 expression is significantly downregulated in lungs of IPF patients, in TGF-β1-activated fibroblasts, and in bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse models. Functional analyses demonstrate that fibroblast-specific Prdm16 deletion promotes the progression of pulmonary fibrosis following BLM treatment. In contrast, overexpression of full-length PRDM16 or its truncated variant (PRDM16 ΔPR-ZF1 ) attenuates the fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, thereby mitigating BLM-induced fibrotic phenotypes. Mechanistically, PRDM16 binds to the promoters of TGF-β target genes and recruits the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex to remove H3K27ac, resulting in silencing of profibrotic transcriptional programs. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal role for PRDM16 in maintaining epigenomic homeostasis during pulmonary fibrosis and underscore its potential as a promising therapeutic target for IPF.

title: On the archaeological evidence for prehistoric human impacts on Tibetan antelope populations
Reply to: on the archaeological evidence for prehistoric human impacts on Tibetan antelope populations
The role of microbial enzymes in intervention strategies for metabolic diseases targeting the gut microbiota
abstract: Metabolic diseases-including obesity, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), atherosclerosis (AS), and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)-pose a significant global health crisis due to their rapidly increasing prevalence. The therapeutic potential of the gut microbiota and its metabolites is gaining recognition, with microbial enzymes playing a pivotal role. These enzymes catabolize dietary fibers into mono- and oligo-saccharides, ultimately yielding beneficial short-chain fatty acids, while concurrently converting phytochemicals into absorbable, bioactive small molecules. An increasing array of small-molecule agonists and inhibitors has been developed to target microbial pathways, such as bile acid metabolism and trimethylamine formation. Furthermore, engineered bacteria and fecal microbiota transplantation are gaining traction as promising therapeutic strategies. This review synthesizes evidence on how microbial enzymes underpin these diverse interventions, aiming to advance the development of microbial enzyme-based management strategies for metabolic diseases.

title: Gut microbiota in high-altitude acclimatization and adaptation: microbiota homeostasis, double-edged roles, and gut-X axis-specific microbiota reconstruction
abstract: The extreme environment in high-altitude regions presents significant physiological challenges to human survival. With more than 80 million individuals residing above 2,500 m, elucidating the biological mechanisms underlying adaptation and acclimatization is a critical area of research in human health. Emerging evidence implicates the gut microbiota in multi-organ dysfunction during high-altitude acclimatization and adaptation, although its precise role remains under-characterized. The Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, also known as the "Third Pole", offers a distinctive natural environment for investigating these mechanisms. This review summarizes the microbial signatures of indigenous populations and the dynamic remodeling in migrants, highlighting static adaptive baselines and temporal shifts in acclimatization. We integrate clinical and basic research to delineate the double-edged role of the microbiota via complex gut-X axes, elucidate the link between dysbiosis and high-altitude pathology, as well as the protective mechanisms of microbial modulation. Finally, we propose therapeutic strategies focused on restoring individualized, axis-specific gut microbial homeostasis to support high-altitude acclimatization and adaptation.

Maternal β-catenin regulates trophectoderm development in mouse preimplantation embryos
abstract: β-Catenin/CTNNB1 is the key intracellular effector of the canonical Wnt signaling. While zygotic CTNNB1 is essential for gastrulation in mouse embryos, maternal CTNNB1 is thought to be dispensable for development to the blastocyst stage. Besides, it remains controversial whether maternal CTNNB1 is activated during preimplantation stages. In this study, we report that maternal CTNNB1 is required for activating canonical Wnt signaling after fertilization and sustaining robust blastocyst formation. Loss of maternal CTNNB1 causes developmental delay, impaired compaction, reduced trophectoderm (TE) cell number, and developmental defects at E18.5. Transcriptome profiling highlights widespread dysregulation of cell-cycle, MAPK/ERK, and apoptosis pathways. Treatment with basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) or overexpression of Ctnnb1, Erk2 , or Ccnd1 can partially rescue preimplantation defects in maternal Ctnnb1 (M Ctnnb1 ) mutant embryos. Mechanistically, maternal CTNNB1 promotes nuclear accumulation of phosphorylated ERK1/2 (pERK1/2) and transcription of Ccnd1 to sustain TE proliferation and robust blastocyst formation. Taken together, our findings shed light on the role of maternal CTNNB1 signaling in supporting preimplantation embryo quality in mammals.
